newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi blue chips end 4.0 pct up on budget euphoria.
newsitem.headline: Delhi blue chips end 4.0 pct up on budget euphoria.

text.p: Delhi shares ended sharply higher on Saturday, as investors went on a buying spree after a market-friendly federal budget, traders said.

They said the Delhi bourse's benchmark stocks index climbed 31.87 points -- nearly four percent -- to close at 811.83 points, as funds and speculators bid after taxes were slashed in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget announced late on Friday.

"The market was flooded with buyers on expectations that the prevailing buoyancy is likely to be maintained for some more days before we see a correction in prices," said Suresh Aggarwal at brokers Jai Mata Securities.
"The index has shot up by more than 60 points in just two sessions," Aggarwal said.
Traders said foreign and domestic funds were aggressive bidders in leading blue chips after the budget announcments beat market expectations.
Market-friendly measures included the withdrawal of a tax on income from company dividends and a proposal allowing companies to buy back their own shares.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram also hiked the investment limit in firms for foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and diluted the minimum alternate tax (MAT).
Shares of Reliance Industries gained 15.50 rupees to 310. Cement maker ACC surged 107 rupees to 1,672.
Auto stocks TELCO and Bajaj Auto were also gainers. TELCO was up 24 rupees at 385 while Bajaj jumped 75 rupees to 1015.
Shares of ITC climbed 20 rupees to 445.
